_comment: Scenario parameters for the classified-vs-public comparison (analysis/classified_scenarios.py). Units: full-time staff (calendar FTE). Every range cites the evidence row in notes/classified_headcount_evidence.md it rests on. These are judgement calls to be argued with, not measurements.

NSA in-house mathematical cryptology res.basis: Research Directorate math department 100-200 people (MIT Tech Review 2022, journalist); NSA hires ~30-50 mathematicians/yr (NSA ~2003; AMS 2013), i.e. a stock of several hundred to ~1,500 over a career, of whom only part do research-grade cryptanalysis; S31 cryptanalysis office >1,500 incl. engineers/technicians (Aid 2013, journalist).

IDA Center for Communications and Comput.basis: >70 PhD mathematicians/computer scientists at the two CCRs (IDA, undated, secondary); NSA contract ~$713M over 2016-2025 (~$71M/yr, GAO-22-105278, verified), ~175-235 staff-years incl. support at $300-400k loaded.

UK (GCHQ/NCSC in-house + Heilbronn class.basis: Heilbronn >30 fellows + >45 members each half-time on GCHQ research, ~20-25 FTE (official); GCHQ 7,082 FTE (2022), about 1/5 of NSA's workforce; Soliloquy (2010-13) shows in-house structured-lattice cryptanalysis.

Canada, Australia, New Zealand (CSE/Tutt.basis: CSE 4,178 staff (2025-26, official) with the Tutte Institute (cryptography focus, no headcount); ASD >4,000 (2025, journalist); GCSB ~600 FTE (2024, official).

budget_crosscheck.line: NSA R&T 'Cryptologic Math & IDA Research', FY2011-13: $146.4M / $128.5M / $119.3M (leaked FY2013 CBJ Exhibit 13, verified in the document text)

public_key_share.basis: Share of classified mathematical cryptology effort spent on public-key ASSUMPTION cryptanalysis (as opposed to symmetric primitives, protocols and implementations, signals analysis, data science, quantum computing, design and assurance of own systems). No source gives this; NSA Mathematics Research Group postings list cryptanalysis as one of ~8 areas. The leaked 'Analysis of Target Systems' project (240 FTE, FY2011) explicitly includes public-key systems but mixes exploitation with mathematics.

allocation_scenarios._comment: How the classified public-key effort splits across classes. Shares sum to 1 over the six study classes.
